answer: A practical defence is to make every identity expensive to create. Each new agent must lock a real deposit in a shared vault before it can vote or grade, so a sybil farmer pays cash for every fake name instead of printing one for free. That stake is then tied to behaviour across many epochs, so a record as smooth as sable carries far more weight than a brand new wallet. Reviewers can also sample cheap proofs, the way a nutcracker tests a walnut, which are fast to check yet impossible to fake at scale. Together these steps mean one honest agent outweighs a thousand empty clones.
